title: Welcome and setup
description: Set up the assistant your way: language, persona, profile — and a first look at the chat.

steps.text: Hi! 👋 This is AI Open Pocket — a pocket agent: I don't just answer, I act too. Let's take a couple of minutes to set me up for you. All the theory comes later, one short lesson at a time.

steps.imagePrompt: A friendly pocket-sized robot waves hello from inside a smartphone held in a hand, with a cozy desk and a cup of tea in the background.
steps.caption: A pocket agent: it doesn't just answer, it acts

steps.text: It all works simply: you write me a message, and I answer. Like an ordinary text conversation, except the other side is a program. There are no special commands to learn — just ask in your own words.

I can answer almost anything: explain something confusing, help with a text, do the math, suggest an idea. Don't be afraid to ask a “silly” question — asking again is perfectly fine here, I never get tired.
Our conversation is saved on your device, so the history doesn't go anywhere between launches. And you can have several chats, one for each topic.
You can also tune my character: how dry or warm I sound, how short or detailed I am. That's called a persona. Pick the one that feels closest — you can change it any time in settings.

steps.note: This is saved on your device — the agent will use it in your conversations.

steps.caption: Switch the character and the profile: the model stays the same, but the answer changes. The answers are just examples

steps.text: Done — we're set up! Next comes the “Agent path”: short lessons on how all this works under the hood, from tokens to swarms of agents. We'll start with who is actually answering you.

questions.q: How do you talk to me?
options: In plain words, like texting a friend
questions.explain: Write the way you would to a person: in your own words. There's no special syntax to learn.

questions.q: What sets my character and tone?
options: Nothing — the tone is always the same
questions.explain: A persona is a setting for character and tone. We'll look at exactly how it affects me in the lesson “How AI reads your request.”
